narration.text: Before we look at debriefs, there are two things to set up.
First, AeroGrid needs to know when you're flying. Open AeroGrid's Model settings and configure your arm switch and flight detection. We covered those settings in the previous tutorial.
Next, open the Edge T X model settings, go to Telemetry, and select Discover new sensors so Edge T X can discover AeroGrid's telemetry values. Once they appear, stop discovery.
Now we're ready to go flying.
After your flight, disarm the model and disconnect the receiver. Once AeroGrid detects the end of the flight, a Preparing debrief bar appears at the bottom of the dashboard.
Give it about ten seconds. When it changes to Debrief ready, go fullscreen and tap the bar.

At the top, you'll see your flight summary. Below that are charts showing your recorded telemetry, with important readings highlighted, for example, your lowest receiver battery voltage or maximum speed.
Drag up or down to move through the charts. When you're finished, press Return to go back to the dashboard.
You can choose what appears in your debrief. Open the AeroGrid menu and select Flight debrief. These settings are saved with the current layout.
Fill from dashboard creates tiles from your existing panels. It replaces any tiles you've already configured.
Tap a tile to edit it. Each tile can show up to three telemetry series. For each series, choose a source and the value you want to highlight: minimum, maximum, average, or change.
Choose Compact for smaller tiles or Wide for larger charts. When you're finished, leave the editor and save the layout.
That's it. Set up your debrief once, and after each flight you'll have the important readings together in one place, ready for a quick check before the next flight.

provenance.status: Native replay on the EdgeTX Companion 2.12 TX16S simulator; review the full video before publishing.
provenance.notes: Uses the original six compact charts prepared for PR #256 from the 10:50 FMS Ranger flight log, supplied separately with --debrief-replay. Recorded columns and statistics are unchanged; Expo is the saved 30 percent, not logged telemetry, and thresholds were not reconstructed. The view and its Preparing/Ready feedback use production rendering. Flight detection and receiver disconnection are explained, not replayed. Dashboard readings are synthetic. All visible navigation and edits use native touch/key input. Visual timing is compressed to match the unchanged narration. The closing holds a finished dashboard frame, omitting the post-save rebuild and fullscreen exit.
